title: SDK rollout admission + idempotent reconciler for tenant-scoped canaries
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need a robust, tenant-scoped SDK surface that lets platform teams create canary/A-B/shadow rollouts without writing brittle orchestration. Current implementation requires callers to implement complex reconciliation, manual retry handling, and permission checks. This causes duplicated logic in client code and frequent incidents when partial failures leave stale manifests.

Goal: Ship a first-class SDK module (go/python/ts) providing: a) admission helpers that validate rollout manifests against tenant quotas and policy; b) an idempotent reconciler utility that tolerates partial failures and network retries; c) compact client primitives for starting/stopping canaries, mirroring, and triggering auto-rollback; d) a permissions mapping and least-privilege operation list for the SDK to call the control plane.

Scope: API surface and client helpers only (no control-plane server changes beyond small guardrail endpoints). Include tests, examples, and migration notes for internal services and partner integrations.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes rolloutClient.createCanary(manifest, idempotencyKey) and returns stable operation id
createCanary is safe to call multiple times with same idempotencyKey: duplicates are deduplicated and returned op id is identical
Admission helper rejects manifests exceeding tenant routing quotas and returns helpful error codes (400 / 403) with remediation hints
Reconciler can detect partial apply (e.g., model promoted but telemetry hook not attached) and finish the operation idempotently after retry
Permissions docs with least-privilege IAM role for SDK consumers published in Console docs
End-to-end smoke test in staging validates canary traffic split, shadowing flag, and auto-rollback triggered by simulated quality regression
design_notes: We opt for an idempotency token scoped to <tenant_id>:<operation_type>:<client_token> (server enforces TTL + dedupe) rather than returning opaque request hashes to reduce client bookkeeping.
Admission checks will run in the SDK preflight against a new /admit-rollout endpoint that returns structured diagnostics (quota_exceeded/blocked_by_policy/warning) so callers can surface UI guidance.

Reconciler will be pull-based: SDK polls operation status with exponential backoff and will include a repair step that runs compensating actions for partial failures (patch subscriptions, attach telemetry, update traffic-manifests).
Telemetry: emit rollout.* events with tags {tenant, model, rollout_id, phase, reason} to tracing and event pipeline for console UX and alerting.
api_spec: POST /sdk/v1/rollouts - body: {manifest, client_id, idempotency_key, intent: 'canary'|'ab'|'shadow'} - responses: 202 {operation_id} | 200 {operation_id} (if deduped) | 4xx structured error
POST /sdk/v1/rollouts/admit - body: {manifest, tenant_id} - responses: 200 {admit: true, warnings:[], diagnostics:[]} | 403 {reason}

GET /sdk/v1/operations/{operation_id} - returns canonical state machine: PENDING, ADMITTED, APPLYING, RUNNING, ROLLING_BACK, ROLLED_BACK, FAILED, SUCCEEDED. Includes last_applied_patch and stable op id.
POST /sdk/v1/operations/{operation_id}/cancel - idempotent cancel call - returns 200 current state
PATCH /sdk/v1/operations/{operation_id}/repair - trigger reconciler repair step with optional dry_run=true
permission_model: Suggested minimal permissions for SDK consumer role:
Admin role retains ability to bypass admission warnings via a 'force' flag
SDK will surface 403s with clear text mapping to missing permission name for faster ops debugging
rollback_strategy: Auto-rollback trigger hooks will be configurable in the manifest with thresholds (error_rate_pct, latency_p50_ms regression, eval_score_drop). The SDK will support both immediate rollback and staged rollback windows (e.g., wait 5m then rollback), and will surface a dry_run remediation plan before execution.
observability_requirements: Emit rollout.* structured logs at INFO with stable rollout_id
Span the SDK client calls and server operations with trace propagation for distributed tracing
Metric: rollout.apply.latency (histogram), rollout.failures (counter by reason), next_op_dedupe_hits (counter)
Console will provide a lightweight timeline view derived from rollout.* events
test_plan: Unit tests: idempotency token handling, local admit decision matrix, permission error handling
Integration: staging run that creates a canary, simulates degraded eval score to assert auto-rollback behavior
Chaos: inject partial network failure between control-plane and telemetry attacher to validate reconciler repair path
Contract tests: ensure SDK conforms to api_spec and handles all error classes deterministically
migration_plan: Phase 1: ship SDK helpers referencing /sdk/v1/* endpoints in experimental flag for internal teams; Phase 2: enable by default for new tenants and publish migration guide; Phase 3: deprecated older ad-hoc client helpers in runtime lib with 90-day notice. Provide a small compatibility shim that maps old createRollout call to new operation semantics.
